failure_modes.mode: BPR Valve Blockage by Solid Byproducts
failure_modes.cause: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution often generates insoluble polymeric tars or salt precipitates; at low flow (0.45 mL/min) and high residence time (23.4 min), solids accumulate at the valve seat.
failure_modes.mitigation: Install inline filter (50 µm) before BPR; implement automated back-flush cycle every 2 hours; select BPR with larger orifice geometry.

failure_modes.mode: Thermal Runaway due to Mixing Limitations
failure_modes.cause: Reynolds number is 13 (laminar flow); without enhanced mixing elements, radial heat transfer is limited. Local hot spots may form if reaction is exothermic, leading to uncontrolled selectivity loss or decomposition.
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate thermal profile using IR thermography on coil; ensure reactor coil is immersed in well-stirred oil bath with <1°C gradient; consider static mixers if heat of reaction > 50 kJ/mol.

failure_modes.cause: Low flow rate (0.45 mL/min) with viscous solvent at 60°C may cause vapor lock in pump head if inlet pressure is insufficient, leading to erratic residence time and poor conversion.
failure_modes.mitigation: Pressurize feed reservoir to 1.0 bar; use low-dead-volume check valves; monitor pump head pressure for pulsation amplitude > 10%.

single_points_of_failure: BPR Valve — blockage causes immediate pressure spike and potential leak
Single Pump Head — failure stops entire process with no redundancy
validation_experiments: Run 10-hour continuous flow test with simulated reaction mixture (including potential solids) to monitor BPR pressure drift and frequency of clogging events.
Perform thermal imaging of the 24m coil under adiabatic conditions to identify hot spots and validate heat transfer coefficient assumptions.
Conduct pump performance test at 0.45 mL/min with pressurized feed to measure flow rate stability (CV < 2%) and detect cavitation noise.
